donnees.titre: Rapid, Non-Contact, Objective Multifocal Assessment of Visual Function in Glaucoma
donnees.resume: We compared a rapid fifth-generation (5G) objectiveFIELD Analyser® (OFA®) test with two fourth-generation (4G) 8-minute tests in the assessment of glaucoma. We assessed the relative diagnostic power of these three OFA tests, namely two high-resolution 4G tests (wide-field OFA30 and macular OFA15), and a new 5G 90-second test (wide-field OFA30-20). Glaucomatous eyes were classified into mild, moderate and severe based upon Matrix 24-2 perimetry Mean Defect (MD). Diagnostic power was estimated by Area Under Curve of Receiver Operating Characteristic plots (AUROC) and Standardised Effect-Sizes (Hedge’s g) for each category of glaucoma severity. We tested 35 glaucoma patients (11 females), aged 72 ± 6.88 years. Their average Matrix MD was -7.71 ± 6.35 dB. Age-matched normal controls were acquired for the 4G and 5G tests. For the rapid 90-second test combined sensitivity and delay reports typically provided the best diagnostic power. For severe eyes, the OFA30-20 produced an AUROC of 90.4 ± 2.98, which was not significantly different to the OFA30 and OFA15. Hedge’s g was ≥ 2.68 for all those comparisons. AUROCs based upon sensitivity alone were not significantly different. We examined the agreement of the MD and Pattern Standard Deviations (PSD) of the two wide-field (OFA30 and OFA30-20) tests. The significant correlations for the sensitivity and delay MDs were > 0.85, and for PSDs 0.53 and 0.69. The rapid 5G OFA30-20 test was comparable to the 8-minute tests. It may be highly useful in young adults with short attention span and infirm persons who cannot tolerate longer tests.
